transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Kivone.
A big shake up in the tech sector today and on Wall Street as chip giant Nvidia reinstated
controversial president and CEO Jensen Wong following his resignation on news of multiple
affairs, particularly with a woman suspected of spying for the Chinese government, which
raised concerns about national security.
The latest development led Wall Street to recover about half of last week's losses,
and PR Scott Horsley has the latest.
Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Wong as CEO.
Just a week and a half after the embattled executives stepped down after it came to light
he'd had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
The board says in a statement it was satisfied with Wong's candor and ability to lead the
company, that's a reversal of Nvidia's position just a few days earlier.
President Trump says he personally lobbied the board to reinstate Wong, noting the company's
stock had fallen sharply in the wake of his ouster.
Nvidia shares rebounded on news the CEO's return, the broader market also saw big gains,
although some commentators voiced concern about the U.S. president playing such a big
role in the company's decision.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
California Governor Gavin Newsom criticized President Trump's use of presidential pardons
in remarks today.
This comes after Trump slammed the Democrats' decision to commute sentences for those on
death row.
KQED's Laura Fitzgerald reports.
In a political speech at the Department of Justice, Trump denounced Newsom's decision
to commute all 548 of the state's death sentences to life without the possibility of parole.
He called the governor's decision a shocking act of injustice.
In turn, Newsom criticized Trump for his use of presidential clemency to pardon political
allies and wealthy donors.
Donald Trump doesn't oppose mercy.
He sells it.
If you're poor, black or brown, you get the needle.
If you're rich and know Donald Trump, you get a pardon and a personal phone call.
Newsom says Trump's pardons have led to less restitution funds for crime victims.
He also accused Trump of using the pain of victims' families for his own political gain.
For NPR News, I'm Laura Fitzgerald in San Francisco.
The Cincinnati Zoo's Hippo Cove reopened today.
After the loss last week of Fiona the Hippo, Zoo Director David Genecke thanked supporters
locally and globally for their love and support after nine-year-old Fiona died from intestinal
complications experienced from swallowing a zoo-goer's hat.
Fiona's mother, Bebe, who is 27 years old, is still at the zoo, as is her brother, Fritz,
who's four years old.
Zoo officials say they are doing well.
The zoo has added a layer of netting above the viewing windows and has removed all ceiling
fads in the area.
They're planning to have a memorial service for Fiona at some point in the future.
Wall Street the Dow was up 1447, the S&P 500, up 326 points.
This is NPR News in Washington.
Greenpeace Middle East is reporting that the war in Iran has caused more than 600 oil slicks
in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters.
Natural habitats for plants and wildlife, they report, as well as soil quality and food
chains are now under significant pressure.
Virginia and Oregon are suing Elon Musk's AI subsidiary, SpaceX Superintelligence, over
x-rated material.
NPR's Wo Jingnan reports that at issue are sexually explicit images of women and children
made by platform users.
This is the first time state governments are suing the company, which makes chatbot Grok
over deepfake sexualized images.
Like last year and earlier this year, Grok users altered photographs of a large number
of people, mostly women and sometimes children, depicting them in little to no clothing.
Although the company has since put in more guardrails, similar incidents have continued
to happen.
Here's Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield.
When Congress doesn't act, we're forced as AGs to use the tools that we have to hold
the line and force compliance with our existing laws.
Using state consumer protection laws, Virginia and Oregon accuse the company of both misrepresenting
the risk of nonconsensual sexual imagery posed by its chatbot and exposing users to such
images on social media platform X.
Wo Jingnan, NPR News.
Gasoline prices in the U.S. continue falling as millions of hurricanes begin traveling
for Thanksgiving.
AAA says regular, now about $3.64, a gallon, a drop of roughly 65 cents over the last month.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after resignation over affair with suspected Chinese spy
Newsom criticizes Trump's pardons after Trump attacks California's commutation of 548 death sentences
Cincinnati Zoo reopens Hippo Cove after hippo Fiona dies from swallowing a hat
Greenpeace Middle East reports over 600 oil slicks in Strait of Hormuz from Iran war
Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX's AI unit over Grok sexualized deepfake images
U.S. gasoline prices continue falling ahead of Thanksgiving travel, AAA reports
